meta.title: Features - Beamlynx
meta.description: Beamlynx is a desktop database client for PostgreSQL, MySQL 8 and SQLite, designed to be safe to use with AI agents: masking per database, read-only agents, and every query in view.

heading: A database client you can hand to an AI agent
lede: Beamlynx is a desktop database client for PostgreSQL, MySQL 8 and SQLite, on macOS, Windows and Linux. It's designed so an AI agent, such as Claude Code, can query your database without seeing what you've masked.

agents.heading: Working with AI agents
agents.intro: An agent connects to Beamlynx, not to your database. Beamlynx decides what reaches it. This part is early.
agents.caveat: Masking limits what an agent sees, but it isn't a security guarantee. Columns you leave unmasked go to the agent's AI provider, so only show what you're willing to share with it.

queries.heading: Building queries yourself
queries.intro: The same query language the agent uses drives the app's visual canvas.

masking.title: Masking rules for each database
masking.body: You set masking rules for each database. Every query the agent sends goes through Beamlynx, which knows your schema and your rules and writes the SQL itself. A masked column is replaced with xxxxx in that SQL, so its real values never leave the database.

readonly.title: The agent only reads, and you see every query
readonly.body: An agent can't change your data. Only you can run an update or a delete. Each query it runs opens in a tab in Beamlynx, next to a timeline of what it has done. If it needs a masked column, it asks you to change the rules, and nothing changes until you apply it.

filter.title: Masked columns still filter, sort and join
filter.body: The agent can still filter, sort and join on a masked column, with values it supplies itself. If it already knows a customer's email, it can find that customer's row. It never sees the emails it didn't know.

language.title: Build a query one step at a time
language.body: A query is a list of steps joined by pipes. Each step works on the result of the one before. The canvas is drawn from the same steps, so you can type the query or click through the canvas, and the other follows.

joins.title: Joins come from your foreign keys
joins.body: Pick a table, and Beamlynx lists the tables it connects to: the table it belongs to, and the tables that point at it. They come from the foreign keys in your schema. Click one, and it's joined. There's no ON clause to write.

edit.title: Edit results, even across joins
edit.body: Change a value right in the results, even when the result joins several tables. Beamlynx keeps each table's key with the result, so the change reaches the right row. A value that can't be changed says why.

paths.title: Find the way between two tables
paths.body: Name the table you want to reach, and Beamlynx finds the chains of joins that lead there. Pick one, and it's added in one step.

traverse.title: See what depends on a row
traverse.body: Traverse follows every table that points at a table, and every table that points at those, and counts the rows in each. It can also write a delete script that starts from the deepest table.

sql.title: The SQL is one click away
sql.body: Every query's SQL is there to read or copy. You can also write SQL yourself and run it as it is.

keyboard.title: Keyboard first, with Vim mode
keyboard.body: On the canvas, each action is one key: i joins, w filters, s selects. Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) opens the command palette. Vim mode works in the editors.

grid.title: A fast results grid
grid.body: 100,000 rows scroll smoothly. Copy a range straight into a spreadsheet, or download the result as CSV.

facts.heading: Good to know
items: macOS, Windows and Linux, with automatic updates. The Windows installer isn't signed yet.
Your databases, queries and data stay on your computer. Saved connections are encrypted with your system's keychain.
facts.license: Open source under the AGPL-3.0. <1>The code is on GitHub</1>.
facts.privacy: The app sends one event when it opens, and usage stats you can turn off. The <1>privacy page</1> lists what they hold.

closing.heading: Try it on your own database.
